a1.say: Let's solve Read a Matrix in a Spiral, using the Four Shrinking Boundaries approach.

card.title: Read a Matrix in a Spiral

a1.cap: Return all elements of the m × n matrix in clockwise spiral order, starting at the top-left.
a1.say: Return all elements of the m times n matrix in clockwise spiral order, starting at the top-left.

lines: Return all elements of the m × n matrix in clockwise spiral order, starting at the top-left.

a1.say: For example, with matrix equals 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, the answer is 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 8, 7, 4, 5.

a1.cap: Keep four pointers: top, bottom, left and right. Read the top row left to right, then the right column downwards, then the bottom row right to left, then the left column upwards. Each edge read moves its boundary inward.
Let's walk through it with matrix = [[1,2,3],[4,5,6],[7,8,9]].
a1.say: Let's walk through it with matrix equals 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9.

a1.cap: Read the top row. The top boundary moves down to 1.
Read the right column. The right boundary moves to 1.
Read the bottom row backwards. The bottom boundary moves up to 1.
Read the left column upwards. The left boundary moves to 1.
Read the top row. The top boundary moves down to 2.
Read the right column. The right boundary moves to 0.
Time complexity is O(m · n) and extra space is O(1) extra.
a1.say: Time complexity is O of m times n and extra space is O of one extra.

a1.cap: That's the Four Shrinking Boundaries approach. Now try writing it yourself, in Java or Python!
